title: Nationality questions review
focus: Ask and answer about one person's or several people's nationalities, keeping nationality distinct from residence and origin.
targetSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities

exercises.prompt: Write “What nationality is Anna?” in Finnish. Use Anna (“Anna”), on (“is”).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which. Minkä maalainen asks what nationality someone is. The joined spelling minkämaalainen is also used. A nationality is not automatically the country where someone currently lives or the place they travelled from. The complete question means “What nationality is Anna”.
requiredSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
exercises.targetSkill: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality

For these words -lainen/-läinen belongs to the nationality word, not to olla. The complete reply means “Anna is Finnish”.

exercises.prompt: Complete “What nationality are these students?”: ____ nämä opiskelijat ovat? Write the full sentence. Use nämä (“these”), opiskelijat (“students”), ovat (“are”).
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which. For several people, use minkä maalaisia and a plural olla form: Minkä maalaisia te olette? (“What nationality are you?” addressed to a group). Minkä itself does not change. The complete question means “What nationality are these students”.
requiredSkills: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities
exercises.targetSkill: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Use minkä maalainen for one person and minkä maalaisia for several people, matching the person and number of olla. The requested question is “Minkä maalaisia nämä opiskelijat ovat?”

exercises.prompt: Build “These students are Finnish.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. An ordinary plural description uses the plural partitive nationality form: Me olemme suomalaisia (“We are Finnish”). In the taught -lainen words, -lainen becomes -laisia: suomalainen → suomalaisia. A group addressed as te replies with me or omits it with olemme. Keep he when both speakers refer to the same other group. The complete reply means “These students are Finnish”.
